data.body:
## AC4 belongs to a family — noting it before it gets lost

AC4 ("CI distinguishes a transport failure from a test verdict") is **deferred to a separate change
after the timeout fix lands**, per the coordinator. Recording the shape here so whoever picks it up
does not solve it three times.

Three open tickets are the **same defect class**: *"could not determine" presented as "determined
the bad outcome."*

| ticket | surface | what it cannot distinguish |
|---|---|---|
| `antihuman-beefwitted-zebra` (`5bba`) AC4 | Gerrit Verified Gate checkout | a 504 transport failure vs. the change being broken |
| `deistic-conventual-blackmamba` (`d1d4-8c8b`) | CI vote bot | a superseded/cancelled run vs. a genuine `FAILURE` |
| `erratic-sunny-genet` (`1e28-1322`) | Mirror Guard | "could not reach the host" vs. `healthy:false` |

In each, an **absence of evidence** is rendered as **evidence of a negative**, and the cost is the
same: a `Verified -1` (or an ALARM) that sends good work back around the loop and trains people to
retry. Tonight's four 504s each produced a `Verified -1` on a change whose content never ran.

A single remedy may cover more than one — a shared "indeterminate / infrastructure" outcome that is
neither pass nor fail, and which the voter maps to *no vote* rather than to `-1`. Whoever takes AC4
should scope all three before designing, rather than patching the checkout step alone.

Linked `relates_to` both.
